predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Apulia, Calabria and Basilicata, 'would remain firmly under Byzantine control until the 11th century' (the page's core regions)

successors.name: Norman Italy
successors.text: the Normans of Robert Guiscard: Reggio 1060, Brindisi autumn 1070, Bari 16 April 1071 (infobox successor 'County of Apulia and Calabria')

ledger.x: About 965: Byzantine Italy gets a catepan.
1041: the Normans defeat the Byzantines three times.
September 1042: William Iron Arm becomes Count of Apulia.
September 1042: the Norman county of Apulia is organised at Melfi (Guaimar of Salerno's council).
April 1071: the siege ends with Bari's surrender; the catepan Stephen Pateran was imprisoned and later allowed to return to Constantinople.
April 1071: the Catepanate of Italy ends.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Byzantine Apulia
wars.outcome: The Normans beat the Byzantines at Olivento, Montemaggiore and Montepeloso in 1041; William Iron Arm was made Count of Apulia in September 1042; Argyrus beat William near Taranto (1045) and Drogo beat the catepan Eustathios near Taranto (1046).

wars.name: Norman conquest of Calabria
wars.outcome: Robert Guiscard took Reggio Calabria, the capital of the Calabrian tagma, in 1060.

wars.name: Siege of Bari
wars.outcome: Bari was besieged from 5 August 1068 and captured on 16 April 1071; Otranto fell in October (1068 on the Norman-conquest page's account) and Brindisi in autumn 1070; Byzantine rule in southern Italy ended.

certainty.note: The catepanate's frontier with the Lombard principalities of Benevento, Capua and Salerno and the Norman county is approximate; the pages name cities and battles, not lines.
